messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] different results every time ?
parts:
The non-indentical results is a feature when running in parallel as Finn
said.

The issue is that the initial value will have a tiny effect of the
obtained mode, and when the initial value is the previous mode obtained
in that thread, then the fine digits are all random.

You can reduce the dependency of running in parallel, lowering the
tolerance, like

control.inla=list(tolerance=1e-12)

or so. not to worry if the tolerance is to small, as the optimizer will
stop when it cannot improve.


from demo(Bym)

using default values

> r=inla(formula2,family="poisson",data=Germany,E=E)
> rr=inla(formula2,family="poisson",data=Germany,E=E)
> r$mlik - rr$mlik
[,1]
log marginal-likelihood (integration) 1.049806468e-02
log marginal-likelihood (Gaussian) -1.396702828e-06

improved:

> r=inla(formula2,family="poisson",data=Germany,E=E,
control.inla=list(tolerance=1e-12))
> rr=inla(formula2,family="poisson",data=Germany,E=E,
control.inla=list(tolerance=1e-12))
> r$mlik - rr$mlik
[,1]
log marginal-likelihood (integration) 1.921693295e-04
log marginal-likelihood (Gaussian) 1.370727205e-06




H

We do sometimes see very small differences along those lines, at least with simpler models, and as H says it may be driven by tolerance settings.  You will sometimes also get very slight differences if you choose different starting values, even with just one thread, although it doesn’t look like you are changing those. I still find the parameter estimates consistently more accurate than MCMC even with slight variability like this.
